record.paper_title: Negative Circles in Signed Graphs: A Problem Collection
record.original_question: Find a minimum-size family of negative circles whose vertex sets cover all vertices of a signed graph Σ.

evidence.quote: C1–4. Like P4.1–4.1 but for the minimum number, or minimum sets, of negative (or positive) circles that cover all the vertices of Σ.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A signed graph is a pair $\Sigma = (G, \sigma)$ where $G = (V, E)$ is a finite graph (loops and multiple edges allowed) and $\sigma : E \to \{+1, -1\}$ is a sign function on the edges. A circle (simple cycle) $C$ in $G$ is called negative in $\Sigma$ if the product of the signs of its edges, $\prod_{e \in C} \sigma(e)$, equals $-1$; otherwise it is positive. The vertex set of a circle $C$ is the set $V(C)$ of vertices incident with the edges of $C$.

A family $\mathcal{F} = \{C_1, C_2, \ldots, C_k\}$ of negative circles of $\Sigma$ is said to vertex-cover $\Sigma$ if 
$$\bigcup_{i=1}^{k} V(C_i) = V.$$

Assume $\Sigma$ admits at least one such vertex-covering family of negative circles. Define
$$\nu^-(\Sigma) := \min\{ |\mathcal{F}| : \mathcal{F} \text{ is a family of negative circles of } \Sigma \text{ with } \bigcup_{C \in \mathcal{F}} V(C) = V \}.$$

Problem: Determine $\nu^-(\Sigma)$, and characterize the minimum-size families of negative circles that vertex-cover $\Sigma$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears as part of Zaslavsky's collection of open problems on negative circles in signed graphs (published in AKCE Int. J. Graphs Combin., 2018). Web search did not surface any subsequent work resolving the minimum vertex-covering negative-circle problem in general signed graphs, so it appears to remain open.
